question.problem:
Given that $K(t)={\int }_{-1}^{1}(x+\operatorname{cos}⁡(t))^{3}\,\text{d}x,$ calculate ${K}^{′}(t)$ for $t\in R$ by differentiating under the integral sign.

${K}^{′}(t)=-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)(\,$
{{field-1}}$)$
question.worked_solution:
Suppose $f(x,t)$ is continuous on $R=[a,b]\times [c,d]$ and $\frac{∂f}{∂t}$ exists and is continuous on $R.$ Then, the function

$$
F(t)={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x,t)\,\text{d}x
$$

is differentiable on $(c,d),$ and

$$
{F}^{′}(t)=\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x,t)\,\text{d}x={\int }_{a}^{b}\frac{∂f}{∂t}(x,t)\,\text{d}x.
$$

This is known as differentiating under the integral sign.

We wish to compute ${K}^{′}(t),$ where

$$
K(t)={\int }_{-1}^{1}(x+\operatorname{cos}⁡(t))^{3}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Differentiating under the integral sign, we get

$$
{K}^{′}(t)={\int }_{-1}^{1}\frac{∂}{∂t}[(x+\operatorname{cos}⁡(t))^{3}]\,\text{d}x.
$$

Next, let's compute the partial derivative with respect to $t$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂t}[(x+\operatorname{cos}⁡(t))^{3}] & =3(x+\operatorname{cos}⁡(t))^{2}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂t}(x+\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)) \\  & =3(x+\operatorname{cos}⁡(t))^{2}\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)) \\  & =-3(x+\operatorname{cos}⁡(t))^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this back into our integral, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{K}^{′}(t) & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}-3(x+\operatorname{cos}⁡(t))^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(t){\int }_{-1}^{1}(x+\operatorname{cos}⁡(t))^{2}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, let's evaluate the remaining integral. We first expand the squared term:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{1}(x+\operatorname{cos}⁡(t))^{2}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}({x}^{2}+2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)+{cos}^{2}⁡(t))\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}{|}_{-1}^{1}+{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(t){|}_{-1}^{1}+x{cos}^{2}⁡(t){|}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{1}{3}-(-\frac{1}{3}))+(\operatorname{cos}⁡(t)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(t))+({cos}^{2}⁡(t)-(-{cos}^{2}⁡(t))) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}+2{cos}^{2}⁡(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{K}^{′}(t) & =-3\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)\cdot (\frac{2}{3}+2{cos}^{2}⁡(t)) \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(t)(1+3{cos}^{2}⁡(t)).\end{aligned}
$$
